Let me analyze this OIML certificate for water meters.

Certificate details:

- Scheme: A
- Member State: Slovakia
- Date issued: 29 November 2024 (Rev 1 date; the revision history shows rev 0 on 18 Oct 2024, rev 1 on 29 Nov 2024). The signature date is 29th November 2024.
- Page total: 9
- OIML issuer id: not explicitly given (SLM is the name abbreviation; there might not be an ID number). I'll omit or null. Actually the certificate number includes SK1. I'll leave oiml_issuer_id out or null.

Issuing authority:
- Name: Slovak Legal Metrology (SLM)
- Address lines: Geologická 9966/1, 821 06 Bratislava-Podunajské Biskupice, Slovakia; Product Certification Body; Hviedzdlavova 31 (probably Hviezdoslavova); 974 01 Banská Bystrica, Slovakia

Certified type:
- Category: Water meter (category per examples includes "Gas meter", "Taximeter"... so "Water meter")
- Type designations: LXC-15, LXC-20, LXC-25
- Module designation: "Ultrasonic water meter with electronic indication device" — module designation per schema is "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. Hmm, here the module designation is a full instrument description. Actually R49 water meters — the whole water meter. I'll record the module_designation as "Ultrasonic water meter with electronic indication device".
- Description: compact ultrasonic water meter with electronic indication device, ultrasonic bidirectional transit-time principle...

Model family: 3 models LXC-15, LXC-20, LXC-25.

Characteristics from the table (section 3):

| Characteristics | Unit | LXC-15 | LXC-20 | LXC-25 |
- Nominal diameter DN: mm, 15, 20, 25
- Permanent flowrate Q3: m³/h, 2,5 → 2.5; 4 → 4; 6,3 → 6.3
- Minimum flowrate Q1: m³/h, 0,00625 → 0.00625; 0,010 → 0.01; 0,01575 → 0.01575
- Transitional flowrate Q2: m³/h, 0,010 → 0.01; 0,016 → 0.016; 0,0252 → 0.0252
- Overload flowrate Q4: m³/h, 3,125 → 3.125; 5 → 5; 7,875 → 7.875
- Ratio Q3/Q1: R, 400 (all)
- Ratio Q2/Q1: -, 1,6 → 1.6 (all)
- Connection thread: mm, G ¾ B, G1 B, G 1 ¼ B (string values)
- Construction length L: mm, 130/165, 190/195, 160/225/260 (list of options — keep as string)
- Installation orientation: -, H/V (all)
- Water temperature range (temperature class): °C, 0,1 to 50 → {min: 0.1, max: 50}, T50 (temperature class). Hmm — value "0,1 to 50" with unit °C; the T50 is a class. I could record water_temperature_range as {min:0.1, max:50} unit °C, and temperature_class as "T50".
- Maximum admissible pressure MAP: bar, 16 (all)
- Pressure loss class Δp: bar / -, 0,63 bar; Δp 63 → pressure_loss: 0.63 bar; pressure_loss_class: "Δp 63" → "delta_p_63"? Keep string "Δp 63" or "Δp63". I'll use "Δp 63".
- MPE upper range: %, ±2 (at Θ ≤ 30°C), ±3 (at Θ>30°C) — config_level: attribute mpe_upper_flow_range, axis water_temperature, values: {condition: "Θ ≤ 30 °C", value: 2, unit: %}, {condition: "Θ > 30 °C", value: 3, unit: %}. Note ± signs — value is ±2 meaning ±2%. I'll record value 2 with note? The schema's structured value has value/unit/footnote. I could record value as 2 and note tolerance... Keep simple: value 2, unit "%". Hmm, maybe record as string "±2"? Rule says numbers not strings. I'll record numeric 2 and 3.
- MPE lower range: %, ±5 → 5
- Capacity of calculator: m³, 99999,999 → 99999.999
- Capacity of calculator with high resolution: L, 99999,999 → 99999.999
- Scale interval: m³, 0,001 → 0.001
- Scale interval (high resolution): L, 0,001 → 0.001
- Accuracy class: -, 2 (all)
- Mechanical class: M1
- Climatic class: °C, -25 to +70 → {min:-25, max:70}, unit °C
- Electromagnetic class: E1
- Climatic and mechanical environmental conditions class: O (fixed meters installed outdoors)
- Flow profile sensitivity class: U5D3
- Battery: non-replaceable li-battery 3,6 V, life time 10 years → battery_type "non-replaceable lithium battery", battery_voltage 3.6 V, battery_lifetime 10 years.

Display: 8 digits (LXC-15, LXC-20), indication range 99999.999 m³; 9 digits (LXC-25), 999999.999 m³. So display digits is model_level: LXC-15: 8, LXC-20: 8, LXC-25: 9.

Model-level characteristics: nominal diameter, q3, q1, q2, q4, connection thread, construction length, display digits maybe.

Type-level: ratio q3/q1 = 400, ratio q2/q1 = 1.6, MAP 16 bar, temperature class T50, water temp range, MPE values, capacity, scale interval, accuracy class 2, mechanical class M1, climatic class, electromagnetic class E1, environmental class O, flow profile sensitivity class U5D3, battery.

Recommendation: R49, edition 2013, scheme A, accuracy classes [1, 2]. Wait — certificate front says "For accuracy class (if applicable): 1 and 2" but section 3 table says Accuracy class 2. Footnotes: the software table has *) and **) notes. I can include them as footnotes:
- marker "*)": "U represents V; 15/20 represents DN; 10248/10253: 102 represents numbers of software version and 48/53 represent checksums"

Software table — matrix table:
Software versions V1.02, checksum 48 (LXC-15), 53 (LXC-20), 8000 version with checksum 61 (LXC-25). Actually the table: V1.02 rowspan 2; checksum 48 → LXC-15, display "U 15 10248"; checksum 53 → LXC-20 display "U 20 10253"; LXC-25: software version 8000, checksum 61, display "618000". Hmm interesting — LXC-25 has software version "8000"? The footnote says 61 represents checksum, 8000 represents software version for DN25. So LXC-25 software version is 8000? Or 1.00? Anyway record as matrix table.

Matrix tables:

2. Technical and metrological data table — this is already captured in model_level characteristics; but the schema example (R137) also emits matrix_tables AND model_level. For consistency, I'll include the main characteristics table as a matrix_table as well.
3. Dimensions table (Fig 2a, 2b) — dimensions: L1, L2, W, H, thread per type. Could include as matrix_tables.
4. Exploded view parts lists — probably too detailed; could include as matrix_tables but it's parts lists. I might include them as matrix tables named "exploded_view_parts_lxc_15_20" and "exploded_view_parts_lxc_25". Hmm, this might be noise. The schema says matrix_tables preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. Parts lists fit nowhere else; I could include them but they're long. I'll include them for fidelity? The instruction 6 about components: "include ONLY if cert names sub-assemblies". The parts list names sub-assemblies (ultrasonic transducer, temperature sensor, lithium battery, PCB, etc.). Components role... The components are generic part names, not type designations. I think including components with role "component" would be over-extraction. I'll include the parts lists as matrix_tables instead — maybe abbreviated. Actually, let me include them as matrix_tables with name, columns, rows. That preserves data without fabricating component type designations.

Hmm, but that adds a lot of bulk. The guidance: "preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere". Parts lists are multi-dim tables. I'll include both exploded view parts lists.

Also dimensions table: LXC-15: DN 15, L1 130/165, L2 106 (rowspan), W 94, H 60.35, thread G ¾ B; LXC-20: DN 20, L1 190/195, L2 106, W 94, H 60.35, G1 B; LXC-25: DN 25, L1 114, L2 225, W 96, H 110, G 1 ¼ B.

Note LXC-25 L1 114 in Fig 2b but section 3 says construction length 160/225/260 for LXC-25. Keep both as stated.

Now build characteristics.

- ratio_q3_q1: value 400, unit null (unit "R" given in table — R is ratio. unit_symbol "R"). I'll use unit_symbol "R"? The unit column says "R". Hmm, ratio unit symbol — could keep null or "R". I'll keep "R".

Note table says capacity of calculator 99999.999 for all... slight conflict; keep description-based values as model-level, and calculator_capacity from the table type-level. Hmm, conflict: the table says capacity of calculator 99999,999 m³ colspan 3, but description says LXC-25 has 9 digits, 999999.999 m³. That's a real inconsistency in the cert (or the table is approximate). I'll record both as they appear; the table type-level capacity 99999.999 and model-level indication range from description. Actually let me add software to model_level too — checksum numeric 48, 53, 61; software_version string. I'll include both in matrix table; and skip model_level for software to avoid redundancy. Hmm. The R137 example explicitly populated model_level for the matrix table values. For safety I'll do both for the main metrological table: matrix_tables entry + model_level. For software table: matrix_tables entry + maybe model_level entries software_version, software_checksum. I'll include them.

Actually, to keep response size manageable, I'll include matrix_tables for: metrological data, software versions, dimensions (15/20), dimensions (25) — or combine dimensions into one matrix table with all three types? The Fig 2a/2b tables are separate; L2/W/H are shared for 15/20. I'll make one "dimensions" matrix table with rows for each model, using L1 from section 3?
